report.summary: Reviewed scheduler.py chunk 1 of 2; claims enumerated with verdicts; risks noted.
risks: dispatch docstring | high | Claims 'STILL sequential here' but code may run parallel advisory tasks when parallel=True; verify intended behavior.
gate_concurrent_writes docstring | high | Describes concurrent execution and TaskAttempt isolation, but method body is not in this chunk; uncheckable.
gate_concurrent_writes docstring | medium | 'cancel forwarded unchanged' is cut off; uncheckable in this chunk.
accept docstring | medium | Claims 'only low-risk work' but acceptance depends only on provider lane; risk model is in Policy, not visible here.
dispatch docstring | medium | 'parallel=True currently overlaps advisory-only work' is consistent with code; but the note about sequential writes may be misleading.
max_parallel_writes comment | medium | Claims full re-index per write and cache lock by root; these dependencies are external (offload.py, structcore/index.py), uncheckable here.

handoff.purpose: Defines KairosScheduler, Assignment, acceptance, planning, dispatch, and write-gating entry points.

symbols.name: FREE_LANES
symbols.note: Tuple of provider lanes allowed for dispatch: ollama, deepseek, codex_cli.

symbols.name: DEFAULT_AVAILABILITY
symbols.note: Default availability dict: claude_cli/ollama True, deepseek/codex_cli False.

symbols.name: _paths_overlap
symbols.note: Checks for duplicate declared write paths across assignments; normalizes backslashes.

symbols.name: Assignment
symbols.note: Dataclass holding task routing metadata: objective, paths, owner, lane, worker, mode, accepted, reason.

symbols.name: KairosScheduler
symbols.note: Dataclass scheduler with bounded concurrency, policy loading, acceptance, planning, dispatch, and write-gating methods.

symbols.name: __post_init__
symbols.note: Initializes bench cycle; loads project policy and overrides max_workers, max_parallel_writes, active_agents.

symbols.name: accept
symbols.note: Routes each task via route_and_select; bounces non-free-lane tasks to Adam, accepts free-lane tasks.

symbols.name: plan
symbols.note: Dry-run acceptance summary: assignments, spawned count, bounced count, waves.

symbols.name: dispatch
symbols.note: Runs accepted tasks; dry_run stops at planning; sequential by default; parallel only for advisory-only work without writes.

symbols.name: gate_concurrent_writes
symbols.note: Docstring describes concurrent write gating via TaskAttempt; body not in this chunk (declared later).

symbols.name: _bounced_or_planned
symbols.note: Nested in dispatch; returns bounced or planned result dict, or None if live.

symbols.name: _run_one
symbols.note: Nested in dispatch; calls offload() and builds result dict with wrote status.

claims.text: Kairos never talks to the user
claims.why: No user-facing I/O in this chunk; cannot observe calls to input/print or UI elsewhere.

claims.text: Kairos never decides trust
claims.why: Trust decisions may be embedded in Policy or route_and_select; not visible here.

claims.text: bounces anything that belongs to the senior crew back to the trusted orchestration layer
claims.why: accept() bounces tasks whose provider is not in FREE_LANES with reason 'belongs to the senior crew -> return to Adam' (line 132).

claims.text: dynamically spawns local workers from a bounded pool
claims.why: dispatch() uses ThreadPoolExecutor with max_workers and calls offload() which spawns workers; bounded by max_workers.

claims.text: the Chinese DeepSeek bench stays dormant without a key
claims.why: DEFAULT_AVAILABILITY sets deepseek False (line 51).

claims.text: enforces their *reduced rights* (the Ollama write-guard already refuses device/vendor/secret/high-risk paths)
claims.why: Write-guard enforcement is in provider/offload layers, not in this chunk.

claims.text: returns a consolidated report for Adam / the owning specialist to review
claims.why: dispatch() returns a list of result dicts including owner, objective, status, wrote; a consolidated report.

claims.text: Default posture: local bench on, external benches dormant (no DeepSeek key, Codex only when the CLI is detected by doctor at dispatch time).
claims.why: DEFAULT_AVAILABILITY sets ollama True, deepseek False, codex_cli False; doctor detection is external but the default matches the claim.

claims.text: This is not a proof of write isolation: an agent may touch an undeclared path. Production write concurrency therefore remains disabled until each task owns a separate Forge workcell/worktree.
claims.why: The function only checks declared paths; dispatch() explicitly avoids parallel writes and references worktree isolation.

claims.text: Concurrency cap SPECIFICALLY for gate_concurrent_writes ... every concurrent write-mode offload() triggers a FULL structcore re-index ... cache's single-flight lock is keyed by RESOLVED ROOT ... N UNSHARED full re-index builds competing for CPU/RAM at once. NOT MEASURED ... default stays low
claims.why: The claims about offload.py and structcore/index.py are external; this chunk only sets max_parallel_writes=2.

claims.text: Only low-risk work that Adam would offload is taken; anything that routes back to Claude is bounced to Adam.
claims.why: accept() bounces tasks whose provider is not in FREE_LANES (which includes claude_cli) with reason 'belongs to the senior crew -> return to Adam'.

claims.text: repo_root makes the target repo's own .agentenv/agents/ roster visible to routing (without it only global agents route).
claims.why: The roster visibility depends on route_and_select's implementation, not visible here.

claims.text: Dry run: who gets spawned, in how many bounded waves.
claims.why: plan() returns assignments, spawned count, bounced count, and waves computed as ceil(spawned / max_workers).

claims.text: dry_run stops at the spawn plan; live actually invokes each bench worker through the provider seam.
claims.why: In dispatch(), if dry_run True, _bounced_or_planned returns 'planned'; otherwise _run_one calls offload() which invokes the worker.

claims.text: Sequential by default (parallel=False): each live write is verified by diffing a WHOLE-repo content-hash snapshot around that one run (offload._repo_snapshot), which catches even writes outside --paths -- but two such runs on one repo concurrently would cross-attribute disk_changed.
claims.why: dispatch() sets can_parallel = parallel and not has_writes; default parallel=False means writes are sequential; the whole-repo snapshot behavior is in offload, but the sequential default is kept.

claims.text: parallel=True currently overlaps advisory-only work. Declared path disjointness is not a security boundary ... Writable concurrency stays sequential with whole-repository snapshots until Forge gives every attempt its own workcell/worktree.
claims.why: dispatch() allows parallel only when not has_writes (advisory-only), and otherwise runs sequential; the comment about workcells is consistent.

claims.text: STILL sequential here, but the reason changed: the isolation now EXISTS -- see gate_concurrent_writes() below, which runs each write through daedalus.spine.attempt.TaskAttempt (its own worktree, its own hardened patch capture) fanned out concurrently, and daedalus.kairos.gated_writes.promote_candidates(), which lands gated candidates one at a time behind a cross-process lock with cumulative re-gating.
claims.why: The claim about gate_concurrent_writes and promote_candidates is about methods in other files; this chunk only shows the dispatch method which does not call them.

claims.text: What THAT path returns is not what this one returns, though: a gated PatchArtifact the primary checkout never saw, not a live write already sitting in repo_root's working tree.
claims.why: The return shape of gate_concurrent_writes is not visible in this chunk.

claims.text: dispatch() keeps its existing auto-land contract for a single write (offload() has always auto-landed a sequential one), and does not silently switch write-mode dispatch to the gated-candidate shape -- that is a product decision ...
claims.why: dispatch() never calls gate_concurrent_writes and always runs writes sequentially via _run_one -> offload, so it does not switch to gated-candidate shape.

claims.text: Every write task in tasks runs CONCURRENTLY, each through daedalus.spine.attempt.TaskAttempt in its own worktree (offload() as the runner -- its verify+rollback cascade stays the authority for per-task correctness; see daedalus.kairos.gated_writes._relay_gate).
claims.why: The method body is not in this chunk; only the docstring is present.

claims.text: Returns one daedalus.kairos.gated_writes.GatedCandidate per accepted write task: a gate verdict plus a PatchArtifact when clean.
claims.why: Return type not visible in this chunk.

claims.text: The primary checkout at repo_root is NEVER touched by this call -- that is TaskAttempt's own structural guarantee (see tests/test_spine_attempt.py::test_happy_path_artifact_and_primary_untouched).
claims.why: Test and TaskAttempt behavior are external to this chunk.

claims.text: Advisory-only tasks are bounced (this method only accepts write-mode work; use plan/accept for the routing verdict on the rest of a mixed task list, or dispatch to actually run them).
claims.why: Method body not present to verify bounce behavior.

claims.text: cancel, when given, is forwarded unchanged to ...
claims.why: The sentence is cut off; forwarding behavior not visible.

observations.what: dispatch() allows parallel advisory-only tasks when parallel=True, but the docstring's long comment may mislead readers into thinking it is always sequential.
accept() treats any provider not in FREE_LANES as 'belongs to the senior crew', which includes claude_cli but also any future non-free lane; this is a broad bounce.
max_parallel_writes is set but never used in this chunk; it is only referenced in comments and __post_init__.
The gate_concurrent_writes method body is not present in this chunk, making its docstring claims uncheckable.
